from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 6  # sources
    J = 8  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [157, 152, 85, 161, 235, 222]
    demands = [45, 34, 17, 25, 39, 59, 17, 36]
    cost_matrix = [[24.05, 17.58, 4.81, 5.93, 29.3, 26.25, 26.36, 23.52], [24.54, 18.72, 12.39, 28.45, 20.73, 24.25, 27.46, 10.64], [21.0, 22.12, 25.64, 11.23, 22.75, 24.04, 3.95, 7.65], [10.05, 27.89, 15.7, 15.49, 27.32, 20.61, 26.59, 23.26], [9.23, 11.53, 26.56, 5.92, 21.97, 24.89, 5.24, 16.8], [24.47, 26.9, 10.88, 27.73, 20.1, 25.46, 18.09, 27.6]]
    emission_matrix = [[6.42, 15.27, 8.37, 11.73, 4.23, 5.6, 17.19, 10.76], [16.62, 4.18, 4.72, 3.41, 11.98, 2.58, 9.23, 18.31], [12.07, 6.14, 15.17, 10.94, 8.09, 11.24, 19.97, 12.93], [20.0, 12.13, 19.26, 6.55, 11.92, 15.19, 3.29, 7.97], [6.86, 15.17, 9.76, 15.09, 5.28, 8.93, 15.45, 3.07], [17.06, 3.57, 10.84, 1.0, 5.56, 15.1, 12.79, 9.59]]
    fixed_costs = [[110, 256, 271, 151, 131, 126, 62, 212], [172, 105, 231, 238, 220, 77, 236, 63], [196, 110, 254, 185, 275, 223, 64, 292], [109, 247, 239, 105, 133, 182, 57, 122], [168, 187, 203, 176, 99, 223, 136, 107], [289, 243, 225, 71, 195, 195, 251, 127]]
    moq = [[9, 13, 16, 12, 19, 12, 7, 12], [8, 7, 12, 8, 15, 19, 13, 14], [18, 14, 13, 9, 15, 18, 17, 9], [16, 19, 8, 15, 9, 12, 20, 19], [13, 13, 17, 10, 17, 20, 10, 14], [15, 9, 6, 8, 19, 8, 12, 16]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Executive Supply Chain Leadership
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: Today
Subject: Balancing transportation cost and carbon impact under practical shipping rules

Context
Our network ships product from multiple warehouses to multiple stores. Each shipping lane carries both a monetary cost per unit and a carbon emission rate per unit. In many cases, the lowest-cost lanes are also the most carbon-intensive, while cleaner lanes can be more expensive. Balancing cost efficiency with environmental impact is central to our brand commitments and our margin targets; we must explicitly account for both when selecting routes and allocating volumes.

Operational rules we must honor
- Route activation costs: Launching any shipping lane requires a fixed setup charge that covers carrier onboarding, contractual fees, and operational preparation. A lane is either in use or not; if in use, the setup charge applies regardless of how much we ship on that lane.
- Minimum order quantities: Once a lane is in use, we must move at least a stated minimum quantity through it to justify dock time, equipment allocation, and carrier commitments. Partial loads that fall below this threshold are not accepted.
- Supplier limits per store: For receiving efficiency, vendor management, and contractual reasons, each store can accept deliveries from only a limited number of warehouses. This cap reduces yard congestion and simplifies scheduling, but it also constrains how we diversify supply.

Supply and demand
Warehouses have finite inventory available for outbound shipments, and stores have minimum demand that must be satisfied to protect in-stock rates and revenue. Our plan cannot exceed supply at any warehouse and must cover demand at each store. Within these boundaries, we should concentrate flow on the most attractive activated lanes while honoring the minimum order requirement and the supplier cap at each store.

Management priority: cost vs emissions
Leadership has set explicit importance weights that determine how much we emphasize monetary efficiency relative to carbon impact when choosing lanes and volumes. We will combine total variable shipping cost and total emissions using these weights. Importantly, the fixed setup charges for any lanes we activate will be added in full and are not scaled by these weights. This ensures that one-time activation decisions are accounted for transparently, while per-unit trade-offs reflect management’s stated priorities.

Business goal
We need a shipping plan that identifies which lanes to activate and how much to send on each activated lane so that:
- No warehouse’s available inventory is exceeded
- Each store’s minimum demand is fully met
- Any activated lane carries at least its minimum order quantity
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of supplying warehouses
- The blended total—weighted variable cost plus weighted emissions, with full setup costs added—is kept as low as possible

This approach will surface the practical trade-offs we face: for example, when it is worth paying a higher monetary rate to materially reduce emissions, or when activating an additional lane (and incurring its setup charge) helps avoid running large volumes through a high-emission corridor. The outcome will be an actionable lane activation and volume allocation plan that aligns with our financial and sustainability goals while respecting day-to-day operating realities.

Next steps
- Confirm the data inputs listed in the annex and validate that cost, emission, and setup figures reflect current contracts and market conditions.
- Run scenario tests on the management weights and the supplier cap to understand sensitivity and identify robust choices.
- Review the recommended lane activations with Procurement and Operations to ensure feasibility on carrier capacity, dock schedules, and lead times before execution.
